168	# All of the regexes are cached, to avoid repeated compiling during processing of same task
169	@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
170	def lazy_expr_regex(
171	    expr_config: ExprExtractionConfig,
172	) -> list[tuple[re.Pattern[str], int]]:
173	    # Basic number patterns (no LaTeX)
174	    number_re = (
175	        # Format 1: Numbers with thousand separators (e.g., "1,234.56" or "1 234.56")
176	        r"(?<!\d)(?:"
177	        r"(?P<integer1>-?[1-9]\d{0,2}(?:[ ,]\d{3})+)(?P<decimal1>\.\d+)?|"
178	        # Format 2: Simple numbers with decimal point or comma (e.g., "123.45" or "123,45")
179	        r"(?P<integer2>-?\d+)(?P<decimal2>[.,]\d+)|"
180	        # Format 3: Decimal part only (e.g., ".123")
181	        r"(?P<decimal3>\.\d+)|"
182	        # Format 4: Integer only (e.g., "123")
183	        r"(?P<integer3>-?\d+)"
184	        r")(?P<percent>\s*(?:%|[Pp]ercent|\s*[Pp]ercentage|\s*[Pp]ct))?"
185	    )
186	
187	    # Expressions such as 1/2
188	    operators = [r"\+", r"\-", r"\*", r"\×", r"\/", r"\^", r"\(", r"\)", r"\÷"]
189	    operators_re = "".join(operators)
190	    all_expr_chars = r"[\d\.\s" + operators_re + r"]"
191	    # Expression should have at minimum at least one operator and must start with a digit
192	    expr_re = (
193	        rf"(?P<expr>-?\(?-?\d{all_expr_chars}*[{operators_re}]{all_expr_chars}+\)?)"
194	    )
195	
196	    # Punctuation regexes
197	    full_stop_re = r"\."
198	    comma_re = r","
199	    colon_re = r":"
200	    space_re = r"\s"
201	
202	    currency_units = re.escape("$€£¥₹₽₪₩₫฿₡₢₣₤₥₦₧₨₩₪₫₭₮₯₰₱₲₳₴₵₶₷₸₹₺₻₼₽₾₿")
203	    expr_prefix_re = rf"(?:^|{space_re}|\=)(?:\*\*)?"
204	    expr_suffix_re = (
205	        rf"(?:\*\*)?(?:{full_stop_re}|{comma_re}|{colon_re}|{space_re}|\)|\$|$)"
206	    )
207	    # Expressions must be prefixed and suffixed while, digits don't need suffix and can have currency units preceeded, this is to ensure
208	    # That we can extract stuff like $100 or 100m2, while we don't extract XDY2K as 2
209	    expr_with_anchors = rf"(?:{expr_prefix_re}{expr_re}{expr_suffix_re})"
210	    number_with_anchors = rf"(?:{expr_prefix_re}[{currency_units}]?{number_re})"
211	    expr_or_number = rf"(?:{expr_with_anchors}|{number_with_anchors})"
212	    regexes: list[tuple[str, int]] = []
213	
214	    final_answer_prefixed_re = (
215	        rf"(?i:final answer is)\:?\s*{expr_or_number}\.?\s?I hope"
216	    )
217	    final_answer_prefixed_just_is = (
218	        rf"(?i:final answer.{{0,100}}?)\s+is\:?{expr_or_number}"
219	    )
220	    regexes.append((final_answer_prefixed_re, 0))
221	    regexes.append((final_answer_prefixed_just_is, 50))
222	
223	    answer_prefix_re = r"(?i:answer)"
224	
225	    # Match after the last equals with answer word - require the number pattern,
226	    equals_re_colon = rf"{answer_prefix_re}{colon_re}(?:.{{0,100}}=\s*|.{{0,50}}?){expr_or_number}(?!\s*=)"
227	    equals_re = (
228	        rf"{answer_prefix_re}(?:.{{0,100}}=\s*|.{{0,50}}?){expr_or_number}(?!\s*=)"
229	    )
230	    regexes.extend([(equals_re_colon, 100), (equals_re, 200)])
231	
232	    if expr_config.try_extract_without_anchor:
233	        # If everything fails, try to match plain expr/number
234	        regexes.append((expr_with_anchors, 300))
235	        regexes.append((number_with_anchors, 300))
236	
237	    return [(re.compile(pattern), priority) for pattern, priority in regexes]

240	def make_latex_env_pattern(
241	    prefix: str = "", context: Literal["boxed", "plain"] = "plain"
242	) -> str:
243	    """Creates a LaTeX environment pattern with uniquely prefixed group names.
244	
245	    Args:
246	        prefix (str): Prefix to add to group names to make them unique
247	        context (Literal["boxed", "plain", "fraction"]): Type of content to match inside the environments
248	            - "boxed": Match environments containing \boxed{...}
249	            - "plain": Match any LaTeX content
250	            - "fraction": Match only fractions
251	
252	    Returns:
253	        str: Regex pattern for matching LaTeX environments with percent suffix
254	    """
255	    percent_re_group = rf"(?P<{prefix}percent>(?:\\?%|[Pp]ercent|[Pp]ercentage|[Pp]ct))"
256	
257	    # Define base content patterns
258	    display_dollar_content = r"(?:[^$]|\$(?!\$))"
259	    # Either \ not followed by ] or everything but \
260	    display_content_bracket = r"(?:[^\\]|\\(?!\]))"
261	    inline_dollar_content = r"(?:\\[$]|[^\n$])"
262	    inline_content_parenthesis = r"(?:[^\\\n]|\\(?!\)))"
263	    inline_content_bracket = r"[^\n\]\[]"
264	
265	    if context == "boxed":
266	        # Rewrite patterns to optionally include boxed content
267	        display_dollar_content = rf"{display_dollar_content}*?\\boxed{{{display_dollar_content}+?}}{display_dollar_content}*?"
268	        display_content_bracket = rf"{display_content_bracket}*?\\boxed{{{display_content_bracket}+?}}{display_content_bracket}*?"
269	        inline_dollar_content = rf"{inline_dollar_content}*?\\boxed{{{inline_dollar_content}+?}}{inline_dollar_content}*?"
270	        inline_content_parenthesis = rf"{inline_content_parenthesis}*?\\boxed{{{inline_content_parenthesis}+?}}{inline_content_parenthesis}*?"
271	        inline_content_bracket = rf"{inline_content_bracket}*?\\boxed{{{inline_content_bracket}+?}}{inline_content_bracket}*?"
272	    else:
273	        display_dollar_content = rf"{display_dollar_content}+?"
274	        display_content_bracket = rf"{display_content_bracket}+?"
275	        inline_dollar_content = rf"{inline_dollar_content}+?"
276	        inline_content_parenthesis = rf"{inline_content_parenthesis}+?"
277	        inline_content_bracket = rf"{inline_content_bracket}+?"
278	
279	    # Build list of regex patterns
280	    patterns = [
281	        # Display math environments (allow multiline)
282	        rf"(?<!\\)\$\$(?P<{prefix}latexDisplayDollar>{display_dollar_content})(?<!\\)\$\$",
283	        rf"(?<!\\)\\\[(?P<{prefix}latexDisplayBracket>{display_content_bracket})(?<!\\)\\\]",
284	        # Inline math environments (single line only)
285	        rf"(?<!\\|\d)\$(?P<{prefix}latexInlineDollar>{inline_dollar_content})(?<!\\)\$",
286	        rf"(?<!\\)\\\((?P<{prefix}latexInlineParenthesis>{inline_content_parenthesis})(?<!\\)\\\)",
287	        rf"\s\[(?P<{prefix}latexInlineBracket>{inline_content_bracket})\]\s",
288	    ]
289	    if context == "plain":
290	        simple_number = r"-?\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?"
291	        patterns.append(
292	            rf"(?P<{prefix}latexFraction>-?\\frac{{{simple_number}}}{{{simple_number}}})"
293	        )
294	
295	    # Join patterns with | and wrap in parentheses
296	    latex_env_re = rf"(?:(?:{'|'.join(patterns)})\s*{percent_re_group}?)"
297	
298	    return latex_env_re

301	@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
302	def lazy_latex_regex(
303	    latex_config: LatexExtractionConfig,
304	) -> list[tuple[re.Pattern[str], int]]:
305	    # Pattern for multiple latex environments connected by and/or (also considering oxford comma)
306	    # Create patterns for up to 5 connected expressions
307	    first_latex_group = make_latex_env_pattern("first_")
308	    next_groups = "".join(
309	        [
310	            rf"(?:\s*(?:,?and|,?or|,)\s*{make_latex_env_pattern(f'next{i}_')})?"
311	            for i in range(1, 6)
312	        ]
313	    )
314	
315	    latex_envs_re = rf"(?:{first_latex_group}{next_groups})"
316	    colon_re = r":"
317	    answer_prefix_re = r"(?i:answer)"
318	
319	    # We first match boxed env, for some reason that's the most common case of output
320	    # Then we match the latex with environments, then we try to match the fraction
321	    regexes: list[tuple[str, int]] = []
322	    for latex_re in [latex_envs_re]:
323	        final_answer_prefixed_re = rf"(?i:final answer is)\:?\s*{latex_re}\.?\s?I hope"
324	        final_answer_prefixed_just_is = (
325	            rf"(?i:final answer.{{0,100}}?)\s+is\:?\s*{latex_re}"
326	        )
327	        regexes.append((final_answer_prefixed_re, 0))
328	        regexes.append((final_answer_prefixed_just_is, 50))
329	
330	        # Match with answer word - higher priority than plain latex
331	        answer_re_colon = f"{answer_prefix_re}{colon_re}.{{0,50}}?{latex_re}"
332	        answer_re = f"{answer_prefix_re}.{{0,50}}?{latex_re}"
333	
334	        regexes.extend([(answer_re_colon, 100), (answer_re, 200)])
335	
336	        # Match plain LaTeX - lowest priority
337	        if latex_config.try_extract_without_anchor:
338	            regexes.append((latex_re, 300))
339	
340	    # This ensures that boxed is matched right after the final answer xxxx
341	    if latex_config.boxed_match_priority >= 0:
342	        latex_re_boxed = make_latex_env_pattern(prefix="first_", context="boxed")
343	        next_groups = "".join(
344	            [
345	                rf"\s*(?:\s*(?:,?and|,?or|,)\s*{make_latex_env_pattern(f'next{i}_', context='boxed')})?"
346	                for i in range(1, 6)
347	            ]
348	        )
349	        latex_re_boxed = rf"{latex_re_boxed}{next_groups}"
350	        regexes.append((latex_re_boxed, latex_config.boxed_match_priority))
351	        # Match plain boxed, the issue with plain boxed is that it's impossible to know where it stops, so if there are
352	        # till last }. We do the actuall extraction in the normalization step.
353	        regexes.append(
354	            (r"(?P<first_latexBoxed>\\boxed{.+})", latex_config.boxed_match_priority)
355	        )
356	
357	    return [(re.compile(pattern, re.DOTALL), priority) for pattern, priority in regexes]

362	) -> list[tuple[list[tuple[re.Pattern[str], int]], ExtractionTarget]]:

410	def extract_expr(match: re.Match) -> tuple[str | sympy.Expr | None, str]:
411	    # First combine the number
412	    groups = match.groupdict()
413	    # Expr group will always exist because every regex has it
414	    expr = groups.get("expr", "")
415	    integer = next(
416	        (val for name, val in groups.items() if name.startswith("integer") and val), ""
417	    )
418	    decimal = next(
419	        (val for name, val in groups.items() if name.startswith("decimal") and val), ""
420	    )
421	
422	    is_percentage = True if groups.get("percent", None) else False
423	
424	    if integer or decimal:
425	        # This makes sure we can convert numbers like 0001 to 1. Do note that this can convert 0 to '', so we assume an empty string was 0 and convert it back afterwards.
426	        integer = integer.translate(str.maketrans("", "", ", ")).lstrip("0")
427	        if len(integer) == 0:
428	            integer = "0"
429	
430	        decimal = decimal.replace(",", ".")
431	        number_str = f"{integer}{decimal}"
432	        number = Number(number_str)
433	
434	        if is_percentage:
435	            number = convert_to_pct(number)
436	        return number, number_str
437	
438	    # Otherwise just return the expression
439	    # Remove new lines and spaces
440	    if expr:
441	        try:
442	            return (
443	                parse_expr_cached(expr.replace("\n", " ").replace("^", "**")),
444	                expr,
445	            )
446	        except Exception:
447	            pass
448	    return None, expr

454	def get_last_eq(latex: str):
455	    # This is to ensure that a=1,b=2 is not splitted
456	    if "," not in latex and ";" not in latex:
457	        eq_parts = equation_split_regex.split(latex)
458	        # We only shorten if there are more than 2 parts, otherwise we keep equation as is
459	        if len(eq_parts) > 2:
460	            return eq_parts[-1]
461	    return latex

464	@lru_cache(maxsize=20)
465	def extract_latex(
466	    match: re.Match, latex_config: LatexExtractionConfig
467	) -> tuple[sympy.Expr | str | None, str]:
468	    latex_exprs = []
469	    latex_strs = []
470	
471	    # Get all latex groups (both first_ and nextN_ prefixes)
472	    first_latex_group = next(
473	        (
474	            (val, name)
475	            for name, val in match.groupdict().items()
476	            if name.startswith("first_latex") and val
477	        ),
478	        None,
479	    )
480	
481	    # Get all nextN_ groups
482	    next_latex_groups = [
483	        next(
484	            (
485	                (val, name)
486	                for name, val in match.groupdict().items()
487	                if name.startswith(f"next{i}_latex") and val
488	            ),
489	            None,
490	        )
491	        for i in range(1, 6)
492	    ]
493	
494	    all_latex = list(
495	        filter(lambda x: x is not None, [first_latex_group] + next_latex_groups)
496	    )
497	
498	    for latex, name in all_latex:
499	        name_without_prefix = name.split("_")[0]
500	        group_name = name.split("_")[1] if len(name.split("_")) > 1 else None
501	        is_percentage = (
502	            True if match.groupdict().get(f"{name_without_prefix}_percent") else False
503	        )
504	
505	        # Use modified config if group name is 'boxed'
506	        config = latex_config.normalization_config
507	        if group_name == "latexBoxed":
508	            config = replace(config, boxed="last")  # Use replace to modify single field
509	
510	        normalized_latex = normalize_latex(
511	            latex,
512	            config=config,
513	        )
514	        latex_strs.append(normalized_latex)
515	
516	        try:
517	            parsed_latex = parse_latex_cached(normalized_latex)
518	            if is_percentage:
519	                parsed_latex = convert_to_pct(parsed_latex)
520	            latex_exprs.append(parsed_latex)
521	        except Exception:
522	            latex_exprs.append(None)
523	            pass
524	
525	    if not latex_exprs:
526	        return None, ""
527	
528	    # If we have multiple expressions and all of them are parsed, wrap them in a Tuple
529	    if len(latex_exprs) > 1 and all(expr is not None for expr in latex_exprs):
530	        # To handle solution is: 1,2 and 3
531	        all_elements = []
532	        for expr in latex_exprs:
533	            if isinstance(expr, FiniteSet):
534	                all_elements.extend(expr.args)
535	            else:
536	                all_elements.append(expr)
537	        return FiniteSet(*all_elements), " and ".join(latex_strs)
538	
539	    # Otherwise return the single expression
540	    return latex_exprs[0], latex_strs[0]

573	def extract_target_from_pred(
574	    pred: str,
575	    target_res: list[tuple[list[tuple[re.Pattern[str], int]], ExtractionTarget]],
576	    fallback_mode: Literal["no_fallback", "first_match"] = "no_fallback",
577	    extraction_mode: Literal["first_match", "any_match"] = "any_match",
578	):
579	    """Extracts targets from a prediction string using regex patterns.
580	    Returns first sucesffuly extracted match.
581	
582	    Args:
583	        pred (str): The prediction string to extract from
584	        target_res (list[tuple[list[tuple[re.Pattern[str], int]], ExtractionTarget]]): List of regex patterns and their priorities for each target type
585	        fallback_mode (Literal["no_fallback", "first_match"], optional): How to handle extraction failures. Defaults to "no_fallback".
586	            - "no_fallback": Return only successfully parsed match
587	            - "first_match": Additionaly Include the first string match no matter how parsing finished
588	        extraction_mode (Literal["first_match", "any_match"], optional): How to handle extraction failures. Defaults to "any_match".
589	            - "first_match": Only tries to extract the first match
590	            - "any_match": Tries to extract any match
591	
592	    Returns:
593	        list: List of extracted predictions, with first fallbac string appended if fallback_mode is "first_match"
594	    """
595	    extracted_predictions = []
596	    fallbacks = []
597	
598	    # Get all patterns and sort by priority
599	    all_patterns = [
600	        (pattern, target_type, priority)
601	        for target_patterns, target_type in target_res
602	        for pattern, priority in target_patterns
603	    ]
604	
605	    # Group patterns by priority using itertools.groupby
606	    match_found = False
607	    sorted_patterns = sorted(all_patterns, key=lambda x: x[2])
608	    grouped_patterns = list(
609	        (gr, list(val)) for gr, val in groupby(sorted_patterns, key=lambda x: x[2])
610	    )
611	    for _, patterns_group in grouped_patterns:
612	        # Find all matches for each pattern in this priority group
613	        matches_with_pos = (
614	            (match, match.start(), match.end(), target_type)
615	            for pattern, target_type, _ in patterns_group
616	            for match in pattern.finditer(pred)
617	        )
618	
619	        # Sort matches by end position (rightmost first) and then by start position (leftmost first)
620	        matches_with_pos = sorted(
621	            matches_with_pos, key=lambda x: (x[2], -x[1]), reverse=True
622	        )
623	
624	        # Try to extract from each match, starting from rightmost
625	        for match, _, _, target_type in matches_with_pos:
626	            extracted_match, str_fallback = extract_match(match, target_type)
627	
628	            match_found = True
629	            if str_fallback:
630	                fallbacks.append(str_fallback)
631	
632	            if extracted_match is not None:
633	                extracted_predictions.append(extracted_match)
634	                break
635	
636	            if extraction_mode == "first_match":
637	                break
638	
639	        # If we extracted something or found something and we're in first_match mode, stop processing other priorities
640	        if extracted_predictions or (match_found and extraction_mode == "first_match"):
641	            break
642	
643	    if fallback_mode == "first_match" and fallbacks:
644	        extracted_predictions += [fallbacks[0]]
645

649	def parse(
650	    pred: str,
651	    extraction_config: Sequence[ExtractionTarget] = [
652	        LatexExtractionConfig(),
653	        ExprExtractionConfig(),
654	    ],
655	    fallback_mode: Literal["no_fallback", "first_match"] = "first_match",
656	    extraction_mode: Literal["first_match", "any_match"] = "any_match",
657	    parsing_timeout: int = 5,
658	    raise_on_error: bool = False,
659	):
660	    """Extracts and parses mathematical expressions from a prediction string.
661	
662	    This function attempts to extract mathematical expressions from text using various strategies
663	    (LaTeX, plain expressions, etc.) and converts them to SymPy objects.
664	
665	    Args:
666	        pred (str): The prediction string to parse.
667	        extraction_config (Sequence[ExtractionTarget], optional): Configuration for what types of expressions
668	            to extract and how to extract them. Defaults to [LatexExtractionConfig(), ExprExtractionConfig()].
669	        fallback_mode (Literal["no_fallback", "first_match"], optional): How to handle extraction failures. Defaults to "first_match".
670	            - "no_fallback": Return only successfully parsed expressions
671	            - "first_match": Include the first string match even if parsing failed
672	        extraction_mode (Literal["first_match", "any_match"], optional): Strategy for extracting matches. Defaults to "any_match".
673	            - "first_match": Stop after finding the first match
674	            - "any_match": Try to extract all possible matches, stops after first sucesful parsing attempt
675	        parsing_timeout (int, optional): Maximum time in seconds to spend parsing each expression. Defaults to 3. Any timeout seconds > 0 or not None will result in the function to raise a ValueError if it's called in a threaded environment.
676	        raise_on_error (bool, optional): Whether to raise an exception if an error occurs during parsing or return an empty list. Defaults to False.
677	
678	    Returns:
679	        list: List of extracted predictions. Each prediction can be:
680	            - SymPy expression (for successfully parsed mathematical expressions)
681	            - String (for fallback matches when fallback_mode="first_match")
682	            Empty list if no matches are found.
683	
684	    Examples:
685	        >>> parse("The answer is $\\frac{1}{2}$")
686	        [Rational(1, 2)]
687	        >>> parse("The answer is 1/2")
688	        [Rational(1, 2)]
689	        >>> parse("The answer is A", extraction_config=[StringExtractionConfig()])
690	        ['a']
691	    """
692	    global TIMEOUT_WARNING_SHOWN
693	    if not TIMEOUT_WARNING_SHOWN and (parsing_timeout is None or parsing_timeout <= 0):
694	        logger.warning(
695	            "Timeout is disabled as parsing_timeout is None or <= 0, you must provide \

703	            pred,
704	            target_res,

706	            extraction_mode=extraction_mode,
707	        )

If you need to run in multithreaded environment it's recommended to set the parsing_timeout=None, which will run without timeout (and signal handling). In this case you need to handle the timeouting yourself."
713	            ) from e
714	        if raise_on_error:
715	            raise e from e
716	        else:
717	            logger.debug(f"Error parsing: {pred}", exc_info=True)
718	            return []
719	    except Exception as e:
720	        if raise_on_error:
721	            raise e from e
722	        else:
723	            logger.debug(f"Error parsing: {pred}", exc_info=True)
724	        return []

32	def _call_with_kwargs(raw_fn, extra_kwargs, *args, **kwargs):
33	    """Calls `raw_fn` by merging `extra_kwargs` into call-time `kwargs`, with `extra_kwargs` taking precedence.
34	
35	    This function is used to merge additional keyword arguments with the original function's arguments.
36	    """

50	def get_custom_reward_fn(config: DictConfig) -> Optional[RawRewardFn]:
51	    """Load and return a custom reward function from external file.
52	
53	    Dynamically imports a reward function from a specified file path and wraps
54	    it with additional keyword arguments from the configuration.
55	
56	    Args:
57	        config (dict): Configuration dictionary containing custom_reward_function
58	                      settings with 'path', 'name', and 'reward_kwargs' fields.
59	
60	    Returns:
61	        callable or None: Wrapped reward function with merged kwargs, or None
62	                         if no custom reward function is configured.
63	
64	    Raises:
65	        FileNotFoundError: If the specified reward function file doesn't exist.
66	        RuntimeError: If there's an error loading the module from file.
67	        AttributeError: If the specified function name isn't found in the module.
68	    """
69	
70	    reward_fn_config = config.reward.get("custom_reward_function") or {}
71	    module_path = reward_fn_config.get("path")
72	    if not module_path:
73	        return None
74	
75	    fn_name = reward_fn_config.get("name")
76	    assert fn_name is not None
77	
78	    from verl.utils.import_utils import load_extern_object
79	
80	    raw_fn = load_extern_object(module_path=module_path, object_name=fn_name)
81	
82	    reward_kwargs = dict(reward_fn_config.get("reward_kwargs", {}))
83	    if not inspect.iscoroutinefunction(raw_fn):
84	        return partial(_call_with_kwargs, raw_fn, reward_kwargs)
85	    else:
86	        return partial(_call_with_kwargs_async, raw_fn, reward_kwargs)

90	    """Resolve the reward manager class from ``config`` without instantiating it."""
91	    reward_manager_cfg: RewardManagerConfig = config.reward.reward_manager

115	    Args:

117	        tokenizer: Tokenizer object used for processing text.
118	        **reward_kwargs: Additional keyword arguments for the reward manager.

124	    # Try to get a custom reward function based on the configuration
125	    # user defined reward manager can be registered in custom_reward_fn
126	    compute_score = get_custom_reward_fn(config)
127	    final_compute_score = compute_score
128	
129	    reward_manager_cfg: RewardManagerConfig = config.reward.reward_manager
130	    reward_manager_cls = resolve_reward_manager_cls(config)
131	
132	    default_compute_score_ = get_default_compute_score(reward_manager_cfg.name)
133	
134	    if compute_score is None:
135	        sandbox_config = config.reward.get("sandbox_fusion")
136	        sandbox_url = sandbox_config.get("url") if sandbox_config else None
137	        memory_limit_mb = sandbox_config.get("memory_limit_mb", 1024) if sandbox_config else 1024
138	        if sandbox_url:
139	            sandbox_manager = multiprocessing.Manager()
140	            # Create a semaphore to control concurrent access to the sandbox
141	            _concurrent_semaphore = sandbox_manager.Semaphore(sandbox_config.get("max_concurrent", 64))
142	            final_compute_score = partial(
143	                default_compute_score_,
144	                sandbox_fusion_url=sandbox_url,
145	                concurrent_semaphore=_concurrent_semaphore,
146	                memory_limit_mb=memory_limit_mb,
147	            )
148	        else:
149	            final_compute_score = default_compute_score_
150	
151	    # Instantiate and return the reward manager with the specified parameters
152	    return reward_manager_cls(
153	        config=config,
154	        tokenizer=tokenizer,
155	        compute_score=final_compute_score,
156	        **reward_kwargs,
157	    )

28	@contextmanager
29	def _score_timeout(seconds: Optional[float]):
30	    """Raise ``TimeoutError`` if the wrapped block runs longer than ``seconds``.
31	
32	    A single ``compute_score`` call on a pathological model output (e.g. a long,
33	    degenerate RL rollout that triggers catastrophic regex backtracking or a slow
34	    symbolic comparison) can run for a very long time. Because ``NaiveRewardManager``
35	    scores samples serially in the driver process, one such call blocks the entire
36	    training loop. This guard bounds the wall-clock time of each call.
37	
38	    Implemented with ``SIGALRM``, so it only takes effect on the main thread. If a
39	    handler cannot be installed (e.g. called from a non-main thread), it degrades to
40	    a no-op so reward computation still runs -- just without the timeout.
41	    """
42	    if not seconds or seconds <= 0:
43	        yield
44	        return
45	
46	    def _handler(signum, frame):
47	        raise TimeoutError(f"compute_score timed out after {seconds}s")
48	
49	    try:
50	        old_handler = signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, _handler)
51	    except ValueError:
52	        # Not in the main thread -> SIGALRM is unavailable; run without a timeout.
53	        yield
54	        return
55	
56	    signal.setitimer(signal.ITIMER_REAL, seconds)
57	    try:
58	        yield
59	    finally:
60	        signal.setitimer(signal.ITIMER_REAL, 0)
61	        signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, old_handler)

85	        self.num_examine = num_examine  # the number of batches of decoded responses to print to the console

101	        already_print_data_sources = {}

112

115	            valid_response_ids = response_ids[:valid_response_length]

1031	    def _postprocess(
1032	        self,
1033	        inputs: list[_InternalAgentLoopOutput],
1034	        input_non_tensor_batch: dict | None = None,
1035	        validate: bool = False,
1036	    ) -> DataProto:
1037	        """Process the padded outputs from _run_agent_loop and combine them into a batch."""
1038	        # Convert lists back to tensors and stack them to create a batch.
1039	        prompt_ids = torch.cat([input.prompt_ids for input in inputs], dim=0)
1040	        response_ids = torch.cat([input.response_ids for input in inputs], dim=0)
1041	        response_mask = torch.cat([input.response_mask for input in inputs], dim=0)
1042	        attention_mask = torch.cat([input.attention_mask for input in inputs], dim=0)
1043	        input_ids = torch.cat([input.input_ids for input in inputs], dim=0)
1044	        position_ids = torch.cat([input.position_ids for input in inputs], dim=0)
1045	        optional_outputs = {}
1046	        if inputs[0].response_logprobs is not None:
1047	            optional_outputs["rollout_log_probs"] = torch.cat([input.response_logprobs for input in inputs], dim=0)
1048	        if inputs[0].routed_experts is not None:
1049	            optional_outputs["routed_experts"] = torch.cat([input.routed_experts for input in inputs], dim=0)
1050	        if inputs[0].teacher_logprobs is not None and inputs[0].teacher_ids is not None:
1051	            optional_outputs["teacher_logprobs"] = torch.cat([input.teacher_logprobs for input in inputs], dim=0)
1052	            optional_outputs["teacher_ids"] = torch.cat([input.teacher_ids for input in inputs], dim=0)
1053	        batch = TensorDict(
1054	            {
1055	                "prompts": prompt_ids,  # [bsz, prompt_length]
1056	                "responses": response_ids,  # [bsz, response_length]
1057	                "response_mask": response_mask,  # [bsz, response_length]
1058	                "input_ids": input_ids,  # [bsz, prompt_length + response_length]
1059	                "attention_mask": attention_mask,  # [bsz, prompt_length + response_length]
1060	                # position_ids: [bsz, 3, prompt_length + response_length] or [bsz, prompt_length + response_length]
1061	                "position_ids": position_ids,
1062	                **optional_outputs,
1063	            },
1064	            batch_size=len(inputs),
1065	        )
1066	
1067	        scores = [input.reward_score for input in inputs]
1068	        if all(score is not None for score in scores):
1069	            prompt_length = prompt_ids.size(1)
1070	            response_length = attention_mask[:, prompt_length:].sum(dim=1) - 1
1071	            rm_scores = torch.zeros_like(response_mask, dtype=torch.float32)
1072	            rm_scores[torch.arange(response_mask.size(0)), response_length] = torch.tensor(scores, dtype=torch.float32)
1073	            batch["rm_scores"] = rm_scores
1074	
1075	        non_tensor_batch = {
1076	            "__num_turns__": np.array([input.num_turns for input in inputs], dtype=np.int32),
1077	        }
1078	        if self.reward_loop_worker_handles is None and input_non_tensor_batch:
1079	            non_tensor_batch.update(input_non_tensor_batch)
1080	
1081	        # add reward_extra_info to non_tensor_batch
1082	        reward_extra_infos = [input.extra_fields.get("reward_extra_info", {}) for input in inputs]
1083	        reward_extra_keys = list(reward_extra_infos[0].keys())
1084	        for key in reward_extra_keys:
1085	            non_tensor_batch[key] = np.array([info[key] for info in reward_extra_infos])
1086	
1087	        # Add multi_modal_inputs to non_tensor_batch if any samples have them
1088	        multi_modal_inputs_list = [input.multi_modal_inputs for input in inputs]
1089	        if any(mmi is not None for mmi in multi_modal_inputs_list):
1090	            non_tensor_batch["multi_modal_inputs"] = np.array(multi_modal_inputs_list, dtype=object)
1091	
1092	        metrics = [input.metrics.model_dump() for input in inputs]
1093	        # Collect extra fields from all inputs and convert them to np.ndarray
1094	        # Keep a stable set of keys so downstream batch concat stays consistent across agent loops.
1095	        extra_fields = {}
1096	        default_extra_keys = {
1097	            "turn_scores",
1098	            "tool_rewards",
1099	            "min_global_steps",
1100	            "max_global_steps",
1101	            "extras",
1102	        }
1103	        all_keys = set(key for input_item in inputs for key in input_item.extra_fields) | default_extra_keys
1104	        for key in all_keys:
1105	            temp_arr = np.empty(len(inputs), dtype=object)
1106	            temp_arr[:] = [input.extra_fields.get(key) for input in inputs]
1107	            extra_fields[key] = temp_arr
1108	
1109	        non_tensor_batch.update(extra_fields)
1110	
1111	        # Only include reward_extra_keys in meta_info if rm_scores is in batch
1112	        # This avoids conflicts when reward_tensor is merged later in ray_trainer.py
1113	        if "rm_scores" in batch.keys():
1114	            meta_info = {"metrics": metrics, "reward_extra_keys": reward_extra_keys}
1115	        else:
1116	            meta_info = {"metrics": metrics}
1117	
1118	        return DataProto(
1119	            batch=batch,
1120	            non_tensor_batch=non_tensor_batch,
1121	            meta_info=meta_info,
1122	        )

1147	class AgentLoopManager:
1148	    """Agent loop manager that manages a group of agent loop workers.
1149	
1150	    Args:
1151	        config (DictConfig): whole config for main entrypoint.
1152	        llm_client (LLMServerClient): Client for the LLM server.
1153	        teacher_client (dict[str, LLMServerClient]): Client for multiple teacher servers.
1154	        reward_loop_worker_handles (List[ray.actor.ActorHandle]): Actor handles for streaming reward computation.
1155	    """
1156	
1157	    def __init__(
1158	        self,
1159	        config: DictConfig,
1160	        llm_client: LLMServerClient,
1161	        teacher_client: dict[str, LLMServerClient] = None,
1162	        reward_loop_worker_handles: list[ray.actor.ActorHandle] = None,
1163	    ):
1164	        self.config = config
1165	        self.rollout_config = config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout
1166	        self.model_config = config.actor_rollout_ref.model
1167	        self.llm_client = llm_client
1168	        self.teacher_client = teacher_client
1169	        self.reward_loop_worker_handles = reward_loop_worker_handles
1170	
1171	        if not hasattr(self, "agent_loop_workers_class"):
1172	            self.agent_loop_workers_class = ray.remote(AgentLoopWorker)
1173	
1174	    @classmethod
1175	    @auto_await
1176	    async def create(cls, *args, **kwargs):
1177	        """Create agent loop manager."""
1178	        instance = cls(*args, **kwargs)
1179	        await instance._init_agent_loop_workers()
1180	        return instance
1181	
1182	    async def _init_agent_loop_workers(self):
1183	        self.agent_loop_workers = []
1184	        num_workers = self.rollout_config.agent.num_workers
1185	
1186	        node_ids = [node["NodeID"] for node in ray.nodes() if node["Alive"] and node["Resources"].get("CPU", 0) > 0]
1187	        for i in range(num_workers):
1188	            # Round-robin scheduling over the all nodes
1189	            node_id = node_ids[i % len(node_ids)]
1190	            self.agent_loop_workers.append(
1191	                self.agent_loop_workers_class.options(
1192	                    name=f"agent_loop_worker_{i}" + f"_{uuid4().hex[:8]}",
1193	                    scheduling_strategy=ray.util.scheduling_strategies.NodeAffinitySchedulingStrategy(
1194	                        node_id=node_id, soft=True
1195	                    ),
1196	                ).remote(
1197	                    self.config,
1198	                    self.llm_client,
1199	                    self.teacher_client,
1200	                    self.reward_loop_worker_handles,
1201	                )
1202	            )

1204	    @auto_await
1205	    @SkipManager.annotate(role="rollout")
1206	    async def generate_sequences(self, prompts: DataProto) -> DataProto:
1207	        """Split input batch and dispatch to agent loop workers.
1208	
1209	        Args:
1210	            prompts (DataProto): Input batch.
1211	
1212	        Returns:
1213	            DataProto: Output batch.
1214	        """
1215	        # Attach per-sample priority to the batch (like ``uid``) so each sample gets
1216	        # a globally-unique priority that flows to vLLM request scheduling. Assigned
1217	        # before chunking so chunks own disjoint ranges without per-worker offsets.
1218	        if "priority" not in prompts.non_tensor_batch:
1219	            prompts.non_tensor_batch["priority"] = np.arange(len(prompts), dtype=np.int64)
1220	
1221	        chunkes = prompts.chunk(len(self.agent_loop_workers))
1222	        outputs = await asyncio.gather(
1223	            *[
1224	                worker.generate_sequences.remote(chunk)
1225	                for worker, chunk in zip(self.agent_loop_workers, chunkes, strict=True)
1226	            ]
1227	        )
1228	        output = DataProto.concat(outputs)
1229	
1230	        # calculate performance metrics
1231	        metrics = [output.meta_info.pop("metrics") for output in outputs]  # List[List[Dict[str, str]]]
1232	        timing = self._performance_metrics(metrics, output)
1233	
1234	        output.meta_info = {"timing": timing, **outputs[0].meta_info}
1235	        return output
1236	
1237	    def _performance_metrics(self, metrics: list[list[dict[str, str]]], output: DataProto) -> dict[str, float]:
1238	        timing = {}
1239	        t_generate_sequences = np.array([metric["generate_sequences"] for chunk in metrics for metric in chunk])
1240	        t_tool_calls = np.array([metric["tool_calls"] for chunk in metrics for metric in chunk])
1241	        t_compute_score = np.array([metric["compute_score"] for chunk in metrics for metric in chunk])
1242	        num_preempted = np.array([metric["num_preempted"] for chunk in metrics for metric in chunk])
1243	        timing["agent_loop/num_preempted/min"] = num_preempted.min()
1244	        timing["agent_loop/num_preempted/max"] = num_preempted.max()
1245	        timing["agent_loop/num_preempted/mean"] = num_preempted.mean()
1246	        timing["agent_loop/generate_sequences/min"] = t_generate_sequences.min()
1247	        timing["agent_loop/generate_sequences/max"] = t_generate_sequences.max()
1248	        timing["agent_loop/generate_sequences/mean"] = t_generate_sequences.mean()
1249	        timing["agent_loop/tool_calls/min"] = t_tool_calls.min()
1250	        timing["agent_loop/tool_calls/max"] = t_tool_calls.max()
1251	        timing["agent_loop/tool_calls/mean"] = t_tool_calls.mean()
1252	        timing["agent_loop/compute_score/min"] = t_compute_score.min()
1253	        timing["agent_loop/compute_score/max"] = t_compute_score.max()
1254	        timing["agent_loop/compute_score/mean"] = t_compute_score.mean()
1255	
1256	        # batch sequence generation is bounded by the slowest sample
1257	        slowest = np.argmax(t_generate_sequences + t_tool_calls + t_compute_score)
1258	        prompt_length = output.batch["prompts"].shape[1]
1259	        timing["agent_loop/slowest/generate_sequences"] = t_generate_sequences[slowest]
1260	        timing["agent_loop/slowest/tool_calls"] = t_tool_calls[slowest]
1261	        timing["agent_loop/slowest/compute_score"] = t_compute_score[slowest]
1262	        timing["agent_loop/slowest/num_preempted"] = num_preempted[slowest]
1263	
1264	        if "attention_mask" in output.batch:
1265	            attention_mask = output.batch["attention_mask"][slowest]
1266	            timing["agent_loop/slowest/prompt_length"] = attention_mask[:prompt_length].sum().item()
1267	            timing["agent_loop/slowest/response_length"] = attention_mask[prompt_length:].sum().item()
1268	
1269	        return timing

106	        replica_rank: int,
107	        node_rank: int,

113	    ):
114	        """
115	        Args:
116	            config (RolloutConfig): full config.
117	            model_config (HFModelConfig): model config.
118	            rollout_mode (RolloutMode): rollout mode.
119	            replica_rank (int): replica rank, a replica may contain multiple nodes.
120	            node_rank (int): node rank.
121	            gpus_per_node (int): number of gpus per node.
122	            nnodes (int): number of nodes.
123	            cuda_visible_devices (str): cuda visible devices.
124	            disaggregation_role: PD role, or ``"null"`` for normal rollout.
125	            disaggregation_kv_transfer_config: vLLM KVTransferConfig dict for PD.
126	        """
127	        if disaggregation_role not in ("null", "prefill", "decode"):
128	            raise ValueError(f"disaggregation_role must be 'null'|'prefill'|'decode', got {disaggregation_role!r}")
129	        if disaggregation_role != "null" and disaggregation_kv_transfer_config is None:
130	            raise ValueError(
131	                f"disaggregation_role={disaggregation_role!r} requires disaggregation_kv_transfer_config to be set"
132	            )
133	        self._disaggregation_role = disaggregation_role
134	        self._disaggregation_kv_transfer_config = disaggregation_kv_transfer_config
135	        # Filled by vLLMPDReplica.set_pd_peer for prefill-side routing.
136	        self._pd_decode_peers: list[ActorHandle] = []

143	        # Forward the Ray job id into the vLLM worker subprocess so the
144	        # colocated weight-transfer IPC socket path is unique per Ray job.
145	        # Without this, two concurrent verl jobs on the same node both bind
146	        # the same /tmp/rl-colocate-zmq-replica-0-rank-0.sock and one fails
147	        # with EADDRINUSE; a stale socket from a crashed run trips the same

156	            from verl.workers.engine.utils import enable_full_determinism
157

167	        self.replica_rank = replica_rank

169	        self.gpus_per_node = gpus_per_node

175	        if self.rollout_mode != RolloutMode.HYBRID and self.config.load_format == "dummy":

454	    async def run_server(self, args: argparse.Namespace):
455	        engine_args = AsyncEngineArgs.from_cli_args(args)
456	        usage_context = UsageContext.OPENAI_API_SERVER
457	        vllm_config = engine_args.create_engine_config(usage_context=usage_context)
458	        vllm_config.parallel_config.data_parallel_master_port = self._dp_master_port
459	
460	        fn_args = set(dict(inspect.signature(AsyncLLM.from_vllm_config).parameters).keys())
461	        kwargs = {}
462	        if "enable_log_requests" in fn_args:
463	            kwargs["enable_log_requests"] = engine_args.enable_log_requests
464	        if "disable_log_stats" in fn_args:
465	            kwargs["disable_log_stats"] = engine_args.disable_log_stats
466	
467	        engine_client = AsyncLLM.from_vllm_config(vllm_config=vllm_config, usage_context=usage_context, **kwargs)
468	
469	        # Don't keep the dummy data in memory
470	        await engine_client.reset_mm_cache()
471	        # A sampled <|image_pad|>/<|video_pad|> has no image behind it, and every consumer of the
472	        # sequence assumes it does. Mask them out with the OOV tail, so the policy cannot pick one.
473	        await engine_client.collective_rpc(
474	            method="monkey_patch_model",
475	            kwargs={
476	                "vocab_size": len(self.model_config.tokenizer),
477	                "banned_token_ids": get_vision_placeholder_token_ids(self.model_config.processor),
478	            },
479	        )
480	
481	        build_app_sig = inspect.signature(build_app)
482	        supported_tasks: tuple[Any, ...] = ()
483	        build_app_kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {}
484	        if "supported_tasks" in build_app_sig.parameters:
485	            supported_tasks = await engine_client.get_supported_tasks()
486	            build_app_kwargs["supported_tasks"] = supported_tasks
487	        # vLLM >= 0.20.0 requires `model_config` to register pooling API routes
488	        # (e.g. ``/classify``, ``/embed``); see
489	        # ``register_pooling_api_routers`` in vllm/entrypoints/pooling/factories.py
490	        # which short-circuits when ``model_config`` is ``None``.
491	        if "model_config" in build_app_sig.parameters:
492	            build_app_kwargs["model_config"] = engine_client.model_config
493	        app = build_app(args, **build_app_kwargs)
494	
495	        init_app_sig = inspect.signature(init_app_state)
496	        if "vllm_config" in init_app_sig.parameters:
497	            await init_app_state(engine_client, vllm_config, app.state, args)
498	        elif "supported_tasks" in init_app_sig.parameters:
499	            await init_app_state(engine_client, app.state, args, supported_tasks)
500	        else:
501	            await init_app_state(engine_client, app.state, args)
502	        if self.replica_rank == 0 and self.node_rank == 0:
503	            logger.info(f"Initializing a V1 LLM engine with config: {vllm_config}")
504	
505	        self.engine = engine_client
506	        self._server_port, self._server_task = await run_uvicorn(app, args, self._server_address)

508	    async def run_headless(self, args: argparse.Namespace):
509	        """Run headless server in a separate thread."""
510	        args.api_server_count = 0
511	
512	        def run_headless_wrapper():
513	            with SuppressSignalInThread():
514	                run_headless(args)
515	
516	        def on_run_headless_done(future: asyncio.Future):
517	            try:
518	                exc = future.exception()
519	                if exc:
520	                    logger.exception(f"run_headless failed with exception: {exc}")
521	                else:
522	                    logger.warning("run_headless completed successfully, but it's not expected.")
523	            except Exception as e:
524	                logger.exception(f"get result from run_headless failed: {e}")
525	            finally:
526	                os._exit(1)
527	
528	        self.task = asyncio.create_task(asyncio.to_thread(run_headless_wrapper))
529	        self.task.add_done_callback(on_run_headless_done)

531	    async def generate(
532	        self,
533	        prompt_ids: list[int],
534	        sampling_params: dict[str, Any],
535	        request_id: str,
536	        image_data: Optional[list[Any]] = None,
537	        video_data: Optional[list[Any]] = None,
538	        audio_data: Optional[list[Any]] = None,
539	        mm_processor_kwargs: Optional[dict[str, Any]] = None,
540	        priority: int = 0,
541	        kv_transfer_params: Optional[dict] = None,
542	    ) -> TokenOutput:
543	        """Generate sequence with token-in-token-out.
544	
545	        Args:
546	            kv_transfer_params: vLLM KV-transfer payload for PD requests.
547	        """
548	        if self._disaggregation_role == "prefill" and self._pd_decode_peers and kv_transfer_params is None:
549	            return await self._pd_dispatch(
550	                prompt_ids,
551	                sampling_params,
552	                request_id,
553	                image_data=image_data,
554	                video_data=video_data,
555	                audio_data=audio_data,
556	                mm_processor_kwargs=mm_processor_kwargs,
557	                priority=priority,
558	            )
559	
560	        prompt_ids = normalize_token_ids(prompt_ids)
561	
562	        # Calculate the maximum possible new tokens based on available context space
563	        # This serves as a safety upper bound. vLLM v0.20+ rejects `max_tokens < 1`
564	        # (see vllm.sampling_params.SamplingParams._verify_args), so we require at
565	        # least one token of headroom to be able to generate at all.
566	        max_possible_tokens = self.config.max_model_len - len(prompt_ids)
567	        if max_possible_tokens < 1:
568	            raise ValueError(
569	                f"Prompt length ({len(prompt_ids)}) leaves no room to generate within the "
570	                f"model's maximum context length ({self.config.max_model_len}); need at least "
571	                f"1 token of headroom."
572	            )
573	
574	        # Determine max_tokens from sampling_params or use configured response_length as default
575	        if "max_tokens" in sampling_params:
576	            max_tokens = sampling_params.pop("max_tokens")
577	        elif "max_new_tokens" in sampling_params:
578	            # support sglang-style 'max_new_tokens' param
579	            max_tokens = sampling_params.pop("max_new_tokens")
580	        else:
581	            # Default to a calculation that considers configured lengths
582	            # Cap max_tokens by response_length to ensure tensor alignment,
583	            # and by remaining budget to prevent OOM in multi-turn rollouts.
584	            max_tokens = min(
585	                self.config.response_length, self.config.prompt_length + self.config.response_length - len(prompt_ids)
586	            )
587	
588	        # Clamp max_tokens to the valid range [1, max_possible_tokens]. The lower bound
589	        # is 1 because vLLM v0.20+ raises VLLMValidationError when max_tokens < 1.
590	        max_tokens = max(1, min(max_tokens, max_possible_tokens))
591	
592	        assert 1 <= max_tokens <= max_possible_tokens, (
593	            f"max_tokens {max_tokens} not in valid range [1, {max_possible_tokens}]"
594	        )
595	        sampling_params["logprobs"] = 0 if sampling_params.pop("logprobs", False) else None
596	        sampling_params.setdefault("repetition_penalty", self.config.get("repetition_penalty", 1.0))
597	        sampling_params.setdefault("ignore_eos", self.config.get("ignore_eos", False))
598	        # Inject per-request seed for deterministic sampling when full_determinism is enabled.
599	        if self.config.full_determinism:
600	            sampling_params.setdefault("seed", self.replica_rank + self.config.seed)
601	
602	        if kv_transfer_params is not None:
603	            extra_args = dict(sampling_params.pop("extra_args", None) or {})
604	            extra_args["kv_transfer_params"] = kv_transfer_params
605	            sampling_params["extra_args"] = extra_args
606	
607	        sampling_params = SamplingParams(max_tokens=max_tokens, **sampling_params)
608	        prompt_ids = qwen2_5_vl_dedup_image_tokens(prompt_ids, self.model_config.processor)
609	        multi_modal_data = {}
610	        if image_data is not None:
611	            multi_modal_data["image"] = image_data
612	        if video_data is not None:
613	            multi_modal_data["video"] = video_data
614	        if audio_data is not None:
615	            multi_modal_data["audio"] = audio_data
616	
617	        prompt_kwargs = {"prompt_token_ids": prompt_ids, "multi_modal_data": multi_modal_data}
618	        if mm_processor_kwargs:
619	            prompt_kwargs["mm_processor_kwargs"] = mm_processor_kwargs
620	        try:
621	            prompt = TokensPrompt(**prompt_kwargs)
622	        except TypeError:
623	            prompt = prompt_kwargs
624	
625	        # Add lora request
626	        lora_request = None
627	        if self.lora_as_adapter:
628	            # Make sure we also check that the lora is already loaded in the engine
629	            lora_loaded = VLLM_LORA_INT_ID in await self.engine.list_loras()
630	            if lora_loaded:
631	                lora_request = LoRARequest(
632	                    lora_name=VLLM_LORA_NAME, lora_int_id=VLLM_LORA_INT_ID, lora_path=VLLM_LORA_PATH
633	                )
634	
635	        with RLInsightLogger.trace_state("vllm_generate", state_lane_id=f"replica_{self.replica_rank}"):
636	            generator = self.engine.generate(
637	                prompt=prompt,
638	                sampling_params=sampling_params,
639	                request_id=request_id,
640	                lora_request=lora_request,
641	                priority=priority,
642	            )
643	
644	            # Get final response
645	            final_res: Optional[RequestOutput] = None
646	            async for output in generator:
647	                final_res = output
648	            assert final_res is not None
649	
650	        extra_fields = {"global_steps": self.global_steps}
651	        # Handle abort case: when the request is aborted by pause_generation(abort),
652	        # outputs may be empty. Return empty results with stop_reason="aborted"
653	        # instead of crashing with "IndexError: list index out of range".
654	        if not final_res.outputs:
655	            return TokenOutput(
656	                token_ids=[],
657	                log_probs=None,
658	                routed_experts=None,
659	                stop_reason="aborted",
660	                extra_fields=extra_fields,
661	            )
662

41	def collate_fn(data_list: list[dict]) -> dict:
42	    """
43	    Collate a batch of sample dicts into batched tensors and arrays.
44	
45	    Args:
46	        data_list: List of dicts mapping feature names to torch.Tensor or other values.
47	
48	    Returns:
49	        Dict where tensor entries are stacked into a torch.Tensor of shape
50	        (batch_size, \\*dims) and non-tensor entries are converted to
51	        np.ndarray of dtype object with shape (batch_size,).
52	    """
53	    tensors = defaultdict(list)
54	    non_tensors = defaultdict(list)
55	
56	    for data in data_list:
57	        for key, val in data.items():
58	            if isinstance(val, torch.Tensor):
59	                tensors[key].append(val)
60	            else:
61	                non_tensors[key].append(val)
62	
63	    for key, val in tensors.items():
64	        tensors[key] = torch.stack(val, dim=0)
65	
66	    for key, val in non_tensors.items():
67	        non_tensors[key] = np.fromiter(val, dtype=object, count=len(val))
68	
69	    return {**tensors, **non_tensors}

299	    def _build_messages(self, example: dict, key: str):
300	        """Replace multimodal placeholders in messages with structured content.
301	
302	        This is required by processor.apply_chat_template.
303	        - <image>: {"type": "image", "image": image} or {"type": "image", **image}
304	        - <video>: {"type": "video", "video": video} or {"type": "video", **video}
305	        - <audio>: {"type": "audio", "audio": audio} or {"type": "audio", **audio}
306	
307	        Args:
308	            example: Row dictionary from dataframe.
309	
310	        Returns:
311	            messages: List of messages with replaced placeholder.
312	        """
313	        messages: list = example[key]
314	        # When concatenating multimodal datasets, get will return None for samples without a modality column.
315	        images = example.get(self.image_key, None) or []
316	        videos = example.get(self.video_key, None) or []
317	        audios = example.get(self.audio_key, None) or []
318	
319	        image_offset, video_offset, audio_offset = 0, 0, 0
320	        for message in messages:
321	            if not images and not videos and not audios:
322	                continue
323	            assert self.processor is not None, "processor is needed to process multimodal data"
324	
325	            content = message["content"]
326	            if not isinstance(content, str):
327	                continue
328	
329	            content_list = []
330	            segments = re.split("(<image>|<video>|<audio>)", content)
331	            segments = [item for item in segments if item != ""]
332	            for segment in segments:
333	                if segment == "<image>":
334	                    assert image_offset < len(images), f"image_offset {image_offset} >= len(images) {len(images)}"
335	                    image = images[image_offset]
336	                    if isinstance(image, Image.Image):
337	                        image = image.convert("RGB")
338	                        content_list.append({"type": "image", "image": image})
339	                    elif isinstance(image, dict):
340	                        if "bytes" in image:
341	                            image["image"] = Image.open(BytesIO(image["bytes"]))
342	                        content_list.append({"type": "image", **image})
343	                    elif isinstance(image, str | os.PathLike):
344	                        content_list.append({"type": "image", "image": os.fspath(image)})
345	                    else:
346	                        raise TypeError(
347	                            f"image must be dict, PIL.Image, or path-like, unsupported image type: {type(image)}"
348	                        )
349	                    image_offset += 1
350	                elif segment == "<video>":
351	                    assert video_offset < len(videos), f"video_offset {video_offset} >= len(videos) {len(videos)}"
352	                    video = videos[video_offset]
353	                    if isinstance(video, dict):
354	                        content_list.append({"type": "video", **video})
355	                    elif isinstance(video, str | os.PathLike):
356	                        content_list.append({"type": "video", "video": os.fspath(video)})
357	                    elif isinstance(video, list):
358	                        video = [os.fspath(frame) if isinstance(frame, os.PathLike) else frame for frame in video]
359	                        content_list.append({"type": "video", "video": video})
360	                    else:
361	                        raise TypeError(
362	                            f"video must be dict, list, or path-like, unsupported video type: {type(video)}"
363	                        )
364	                    video_offset += 1
365	                elif segment == "<audio>":
366	                    assert audio_offset < len(audios), f"audio_offset {audio_offset} >= len(audios) {len(audios)}"
367	                    audio = audios[audio_offset]
368	                    if isinstance(audio, dict):
369	                        payload = dict(audio)
370	                        payload["type"] = "audio"
371	                        if "audio" not in payload and "audio_url" not in payload:
372	                            payload = {"type": "audio", "audio": audio}
373	                        content_list.append(payload)
374	                    else:
375	                        content_list.append({"type": "audio", "audio": audio})
376	                    audio_offset += 1
377	                else:
378	                    content_list.append({"type": "text", "text": segment})
379	            message["content"] = content_list
380	
381	        assert image_offset == len(images), f"image_offset {image_offset} != len(images) {len(images)}"
382	        assert video_offset == len(videos), f"video_offset {video_offset} != len(videos) {len(videos)}"
383	        assert audio_offset == len(audios), f"audio_offset {audio_offset} != len(audios) {len(audios)}"
384	        return messages

413	    @classmethod
414	    async def process_vision_info(
415	        cls,
416	        messages: list[dict],
417	        image_patch_size,
418	        config: DictConfig,
419	    ) -> tuple[list[Image.Image], list[tuple[torch.Tensor, dict]]]:
420	        """Extract images and videos from messages.
421	
422	        This method is called by AgentLoop (e.g SingleTurnAgentLoop) before apply_chat_template to
423	        the `raw_prompt` from dataset. User may customize RLHFDataset and override this method to
424	        support custom vision extraction.
425	
426	        >>> messages = kwargs["raw_prompt"]
427	        >>> images, videos = RLHFDataset.process_vision_info(messages, image_patch_size)
428	        >>> videos, video_metadatas = zip(*videos)
429	        >>> raw_prompt = processor.apply_chat_template(messages, tokenize=False)
430	        >>> inputs = processor(text=[raw_prompt], images=images, videos=videos,
431	        ...                    video_metadata=video_metadatas, do_sample_frames=False)
432	
433	        Args:
434	            messages: List of messages from dataset `raw_prompt`.
435	            image_patch_size: Image patch size for processor.
436	            config: Config for dataset.
437	
438	        Returns:
439	            images: List of images.
440	            videos: List of videos, each video is a tuple of (video_tensor, video_metadata).
441	        """
442	        from qwen_vl_utils import process_vision_info
443	
444	        # When called from an AgentLoop, many trajectory coroutines share one
445	        # event loop. ``process_vision_info`` does synchronous PNG decode +
446	        # smart_resize (CPU-heavy); running it inline blocks the loop and starves
447	        # every sibling coroutine's socket I/O (manifests as connect timeouts /
448	        # zero-window stalls under concurrency). Offload to a thread: PIL/numpy
449	        # release the GIL during decode/resize, so the loop stays responsive and
450	        # the work parallelizes across threads. This method is ``async`` and only
451	        # ever awaited from an AgentLoop (which always has a running loop), so
452	        # ``get_running_loop()`` is safe here.
453	        loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
454	        images, videos = await loop.run_in_executor(
455	            None,
456	            lambda: process_vision_info(messages, image_patch_size=image_patch_size, return_video_metadata=True),
457	        )
458	        return images, videos

460	    @classmethod
461	    def _extract_audio_info(cls, messages: list[dict]) -> list[Any]:
462	        audios = []
463	        for message in messages:
464	            content = message.get("content")
465	            if not isinstance(content, list):
466	                continue
467	            for item in content:
468	                if not isinstance(item, dict) or item.get("type") != "audio":
469	                    continue
470	                if "audio" in item:
471	                    audios.append(item["audio"])
472	                elif "audio_url" in item:
473	                    audios.append(item["audio_url"])
474	                else:
475	                    audios.append({k: v for k, v in item.items() if k != "type"})
476	        return audios or None

510	    def split(self, num_splits: int):
511	        """
512	        split the dataset into num_splits sub-datasets
513	        Args:
514	            num_splits: specified number of splits
515	        Returns:
516	            List[RLHFDataset]: list of RLHFDataset splits
517	        Raises:
518	            ValueError: if num_splits is not a positive integer
519	        """
520	        if not isinstance(num_splits, int) or num_splits <= 0:
521	            raise ValueError(f"num_splits must be a positive integer, got {num_splits}")
522	
523	        if not hasattr(self, "dataframe"):
524	            raise AttributeError(
525	                "dataframe not found in RLHFDataset\n"
526	                "reason: _read_files_and_tokenize() not called or Parquet file loading failed"
527	            )
528	        if self.dataframe is None:
529	            raise ValueError("RLHFDataset dataframe 为 None!")
530	
531	        total_samples = len(self.dataframe)
532	        print(f"total_samples: {total_samples}")
533	        if total_samples == 0:
534	            raise ValueError("Cannot split an empty dataset")
535	
536	        # Calculate effective sample count after dropping remainders if needed
537	        if total_samples % num_splits != 0:
538	            total_samples = total_samples - (total_samples % num_splits)
539	            logging.warning(f"Dropping {len(self.dataframe) % num_splits} samples, effective samples: {total_samples}")
540	
541	        split_size = total_samples // num_splits
542	        splits = []
543	
544	        for i in range(num_splits):
545	            start_idx = i * split_size
546	            end_idx = (i + 1) * split_size if i < num_splits - 1 else total_samples
547	
548	            split_dataframe = self.dataframe.select(range(start_idx, end_idx))
549	
550	            split_dataset = RLHFDataset(
551	                data_files=self.data_files,
552	                tokenizer=self.tokenizer,
553	                config=self.config,
554	                processor=self.processor,
555	                max_samples=self.max_samples,
556	            )
557	            split_dataset.dataframe = split_dataframe
558	            split_dataset.serialize_dataset = self.serialize_dataset
559	            split_dataset.original_data_files = self.original_data_files
560	
561	            splits.append(split_dataset)
562	
563	        return splits

140	def create_rl_sampler(data_config, dataset):
141	    """Create a sampler for the dataset.
142	
143	    Arguments:
144	        data_config: The data config.
145	        dataset (Dataset): The dataset.
146	
147	    Returns:
148	        sampler (Sampler): The sampler.
149	    """
150	    import torch
151	    from torch.utils.data import SequentialSampler
152	
153	    # torch.utils.data.RandomSampler could not recover properly
154	    from torchdata.stateful_dataloader.sampler import RandomSampler
155	
156	    # Use a sampler to facilitate checkpoint resumption.
157	    # If shuffling is enabled in the data configuration, create a random sampler.
158	    if data_config.shuffle:
159	        train_dataloader_generator = torch.Generator()
160	        seed = data_config.get("seed")
161	        if seed is not None:
162	            train_dataloader_generator.manual_seed(seed)
163	        sampler = RandomSampler(data_source=dataset, generator=train_dataloader_generator)
164	    else:
165	        # If shuffling is disabled, use a sequential sampler to iterate through the dataset in order.
166	        sampler = SequentialSampler(data_source=dataset)
167	
168	    return sampler

79	def safe_sympy_doit(a: Basic | MatrixBase):
80	    """Safely execute doit() on a sympy expression, catching exceptions.
81	      Doit in sympy will evaluate expressions it will pass the expression tree and evluate nodes.
82	      For example for 1+1+1 it will evaluate the additions and return 3. One issue with it is that it maybe
83	      evaluates too much as integrals will also be evaluated.
84	      As we are using latex2sympy2_extended, evaluates are lazy and only evaluated when needed.
85	
86	    Args:
87	        a: A sympy Basic or MatrixBase expression to evaluate
88	
89	    Returns:
90	        The result of a.doit() if successful, otherwise returns the original expression
91	    """
92	    try:
93	        return a.doit()
94	    except Exception:
95	        pass
96	    return a

105	    """Check if expression is either an atomic type or percentage atomic type.
106

109	        atomic_type: The atomic type to check for

111	    Returns:
112	        True if expr is atomic_type or percentage atomic type, False otherwise
113	    """
114	    return isinstance(expr, atomic_type) or (
115	        # Check for percentage representation: latex2sympy_extended converts "X%" into X*UnevaluatedExpr(Rational(1,100))
116	        # So we detect percentages by looking for this multiplication structure
117	        isinstance(expr, Mul)
118	        and len(expr.args) == 2
119	        and expr.args[1] == UnevaluatedExpr(Rational(1, 100))
120	        and isinstance(expr.args[0], atomic_type)
121	    )

124	def sympy_numeric_eq(
125	    a: Basic | MatrixBase,

128	    numeric_precision: int,

130	    """Compare two sympy expressions numerically with given precision.
131	
132	    Args:
133	        a: First sympy expression
134	        b: Second sympy expression
135	        precision: Number of decimal places to compare
136	
137	    Returns:
138	        True if expressions are numerically equal within precision, False otherwise
139	    """
140	    # Only do this when one of the two is a float, in other cases use symbolic equality as this could lead to false positives
141	    # E.g we want 1/3 == 0.333333 to work
142	    if isinstance(a, (MatrixBase, MatrixExpr)) and isinstance(
143	        b, (MatrixBase, MatrixExpr)
144	    ):
145	        a = safe_sympy_doit(a)
146	        b = safe_sympy_doit(b)
147	
148	        # If we have matrices and one of them is only made of floats, we can use the same logic as above
149	        if (
150	            isinstance(a, (MatrixBase))
151	            and isinstance(b, (MatrixBase))
152	            and a.shape == b.shape
153	        ):
154	            return all(
155	                sympy_numeric_eq(a_elem, b_elem, float_rounding, numeric_precision)
156	                for a_elem, b_elem in zip(a.flat(), b.flat(), strict=True)
157	            )
158	
159	    # Ensure this also works for percentage numbers so that 0.333333% = 0.33333333333 with precision 4
160	    elif is_atomic_or_pct_atomic(a, Number) or is_atomic_or_pct_atomic(b, Number):
161	        # If one of them is a float or a percentage number, we can try to use float precision
162	        if is_atomic_or_pct_atomic(a, Float) or is_atomic_or_pct_atomic(b, Float):
163	            a = safe_sympy_doit(a)
164	            b = safe_sympy_doit(b)
165	            try:

167	            except Exception:

170	        elif is_atomic_or_pct_atomic(a, Integer) and is_atomic_or_pct_atomic(b, Integer):
171	            a = get_pct_val(a, a)
172	            b = get_pct_val(b, b)
173	            return a == b

453	def sympy_compare_symbols(gold: Basic | MatrixBase, pred: Basic | MatrixBase) -> bool:
454	    """Compare two sympy expressions where at least one is a Symbol.
455	
456	    Handles special cases:
457	    - One is Symbol and other is E (limitation of parsed expressions)
458	    - One is multiplication of symbols and other is single symbol (concatenated comparison)
459	
460	    Args:
461	        gold: First sympy expression (expected)
462	        pred: Second sympy expression (predicted)
463	        precision: Number of decimal places to compare
464	
465	    Returns:
466	        True if expressions are equal by any comparison method, False otherwise
467	    """
468	    # Handle E vs symbol case
469	    if (isinstance(gold, Symbol) and gold.name.lower() == "e" and pred == E) or (
470	        isinstance(pred, Symbol) and pred.name.lower() == "e" and gold == E

471	    ):
472	        return True
473	
474	    # Handle multiplication of symbols vs single symbol, because parsing return $abc$ -> abc
475	    # We also handle E as it's a symbol, because E will be always parsed as exp
476	    if (
477	        isinstance(gold, Symbol)
478	        and isinstance(pred, Mul)
479	        and all(arg == E or isinstance(arg, (Symbol)) for arg in pred.args)
480	    ):
481	        concat_pred = "".join(
482	            arg.name if isinstance(arg, Symbol) else "e" for arg in pred.args
483	        )
484	        return gold.name.lower() == concat_pred.lower()
485	
486	    if (
487	        isinstance(pred, Symbol)
488	        and isinstance(gold, Mul)
489	        and all(arg == E or isinstance(arg, (Symbol)) for arg in gold.args)
490	    ):
491	        concat_gold = "".join(
492	            arg.name if isinstance(arg, Symbol) else "e" for arg in gold.args
493	        )
494	        return pred.name.lower() == concat_gold.lower()
495	
496	    # Simple
497	    if isinstance(gold, Symbol) and isinstance(pred, Symbol):
498	        g_name = gold.name
499	        p_name = pred.name
500	        if len(p_name) > 1:
501	            p_name = p_name.lower()
502	        if len(g_name) > 1:
503	            g_name = g_name.lower()
504	        return g_name == p_name
505	
506	    return str(gold) == str(pred)

509	def is_relation(expr: Basic | MatrixBase) -> bool:
510	    """Check if an expression is a relational expression.
511	
512	    Args:
513	        expr: The expression to check
514	    Returns:
515	        bool: True if expr is a relational expression or And of relations, False otherwise
516	    """
517	    if isinstance(expr, Relational):
518	        return True
519	
520	    if isinstance(expr, And) and len(expr._unsorted_args) > 0:
521	        return all(isinstance(arg, Relational) for arg in expr._unsorted_args)
522	
523	    return False

526	def is_equation(expr: Basic | MatrixBase) -> bool:
527	    """Check if an expression is an equation.
528	
529	    Args:
530	        expr: The expression to check
531	    Returns:
532	        bool: True if expr is an equation, False otherwise
533	    """
534	    if isinstance(expr, Eq):
535	        return True
536	
537	    if isinstance(expr, And) and len(expr._unsorted_args) > 0:
538	        return all(isinstance(arg, Eq) for arg in expr._unsorted_args)
539	
540	    return False

544	    """Check if an expression is an assignment relation. E.g a=1
545	
546	    Args:
547	        expr: The expression to check
548	    Returns:
549	        bool: True if expr is a relational expression or And of relations, False otherwise
550	    """
551	    if isinstance(expr, Eq) and is_expr_of_only_symbols(expr.lhs):

555	        return all(
556	            isinstance(arg, Eq) for arg in expr._unsorted_args
557	        ) and is_expr_of_only_symbols(expr._unsorted_args[0].lhs)

559	    return False

563	    """Take the last relation from an And expression."""
564	    if isinstance(expr, And):

570	    """Take the first relation from an And expression."""
571	    if isinstance(expr, And):

576	def unwrap_fcs(expr: Basic | MatrixBase) -> Basic | MatrixBase:
577	    """Unwrap function calls to their arguments.
578	
579	    For example, Function('f')(x) becomes Symbol('f_x')
580	
581	    Args:
582	        expr: The expression to unwrap
583	
584	    Returns:
585	        The unwrapped expression with functions replaced by concatenated symbols
586	    """
587	    # Base case - not a Basic type
588	    if not isinstance(expr, Basic):
589	        return expr
590	
591	    # Handle function case
592	    if hasattr(expr, "func") and isinstance(expr.func, UndefinedFunction):
593	        # Get function name and arguments
594	        func_name = expr.func.__name__
595	        # Recursively unwrap arguments before converting to string
596	        unwrapped_args = [str(unwrap_fcs(arg)) for arg in expr.args]
597	        # Create new symbol by concatenating function name and args
598	        return Symbol(f"{func_name}_{'_'.join(unwrapped_args)}")
599	
600	    # Recursively unwrap all arguments
601	    try:
602	        new_args = [unwrap_fcs(arg) for arg in expr.args]
603	        if new_args:
604	            return expr.func(*new_args)
605	    except Exception:
606	        pass
607	
608	    return expr

611	def sympy_expr_eq(
612	    gold: Basic | MatrixBase,
613	    pred: Basic | MatrixBase,
614	    float_rounding: int,
615	    numeric_precision: int,
616	    allow_set_relation_comp: bool = False,
617	    strict: bool = True,
618	) -> bool:
619	    """Compare two sympy expressions for equality using multiple methods.
620	
621	    Args:
622	        gold: First sympy expression (expected)
623	        pred: Second sympy expression (predicted)
624	        precision: Number of decimal places to compare
625	        allow_set_relation_comp: Whether to allow set - relation comparison. Defaults to False.
626	            - If True, set - relation comparison will be allowed in all cases.
627	            - If False, set - relation comparison will be allowed only if the prediction is a set.
628	        strict: If true, variables do matter otherwise they don't
629	
630	    Returns:
631	        True if expressions are equal by any comparison method, False otherwise
632	    """
633	
634	    # This ensures that f(x) == f(y) is true
635	    if not strict:
636	        try:
637	            gold_variables = gold.free_symbols
638	            pred_variables = pred.free_symbols
639	            if len(gold_variables) == len(pred_variables):
640	                pred = pred.subs(
641	                    list(zip(pred_variables, gold_variables, strict=True))
642	                )
643	        except Exception:
644	            pass
645	
646	    # If both are assigments, we don't want to unwrap them, so that x=1 != y=1
647	    # But if one is assignment and other is equation, we want to unwrap both
648	
649	    # We always want to truncate if it's assignment, assignment
650	
651	    is_gold_assignment = is_assignment_relation(gold)
652	    is_pred_assignment = is_assignment_relation(pred)
653	    is_gold_equation = is_equation(gold)
654	    is_pred_equation = is_equation(pred)
655	
656	    # Truncate equations chains in case of assignment, this doesn't change any of the above values,
657	    # so no need to recompute them
658	    if is_gold_assignment:
659	        gold = Eq(
660	            take_first_relation(gold).lhs, take_last_relation(gold).rhs, evaluate=False
661	        )
662	    if is_pred_assignment:
663	        pred = Eq(
664	            take_first_relation(pred).lhs, take_last_relation(pred).rhs, evaluate=False
665	        )
666	
667	    # We follow what the gold format is
668	    # 1 and 9=1 -> 1,1
669	    if is_pred_equation and not is_gold_equation:
670	        # Unwrap pred
671	        pred = take_last_relation(pred).rhs
672	
673	    # We respect what the pred format is only if the gold is assignment so that x=1 and 1 -> 1,1, but not 2x + z = 1 and 1 -> 1,1
674	    elif is_gold_assignment and not is_pred_equation:
675	        gold = take_last_relation(gold).rhs
676	
677	    if is_relation(gold) and isinstance(pred, Set):
678	        # This is to ensure that 1 < x < 2 equals (-oo, 1) U (2, oo)
679	        # We also unwrap the functions because othewise it creates some conditional set based on the function name
680	        try:
681	            gold = unwrap_fcs(gold).as_set()
682	        except Exception:
683	            pass
684	
685	    if allow_set_relation_comp and is_relation(pred) and isinstance(gold, Set):
686	        try:
687	            pred = unwrap_fcs(pred).as_set()
688	        except Exception:
689	            pass
690	
691	    # Start with simple str and expr comparisson as it's the fastest
692	    # str comparison is better, than simple eq, because it will also handle missarangments
693	    if sympy_str_eq(gold, pred):
694	        return True
695	
696	    # Support for equations
697	    if is_relation(gold) and is_relation(pred):
698	        return sympy_compare_relational(gold, pred, float_rounding, numeric_precision)
699	
700	    elif isinstance(gold, (Set, Tuple)) or isinstance(pred, (Set, Tuple)):
701	        return sympy_compare_sets(gold, pred, float_rounding, numeric_precision)
702	
703	    # Handles $\text{answer}$ == $answer$, one is symbol, is multiplication of symbols (a*n*s*w*e*r)
704	    elif isinstance(gold, Symbol) or isinstance(pred, Symbol):
705	        return sympy_compare_symbols(gold, pred)
706	
707	    elif isinstance(gold, (Basic, MatrixBase)) and isinstance(
708	        pred, (Basic, MatrixBase)
709	    ):
710	        # Mostly so that 0.333333 = 1/3
711	        if sympy_numeric_eq(gold, pred, float_rounding, numeric_precision):
712	            return True
713	        # Then try symbolic equality
714	        if sympy_symbolic_eq(gold, pred):
715	            return True
716	
717	    return False
